verdict: PagerDuty: Choose PagerDuty when paging and incident response are the job — not when you need Datadog telemetry or ServiceNow ITSM. Scores use the IT & Development editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing.
bestFor: SRE/IT teams that need on-call schedules and paging
Orgs already sending alerts from Datadog/CloudWatch
Incident commanders who want a dedicated ops cloud
notIdealFor: Teams that only need APM dashboards (New Relic / Grafana)
tradeoffs: Per-agent vs per-host vs per-seat vs per-GB pricing models
Module stacking and consumption overages vs single-SKU floors
Free tiers vs enterprise SSO/audit gates
Landscape-adjacent tools vs primary job-cluster peers on best pages
recommendation: Choose PagerDuty when paging and incident response are the job — not when you need Datadog telemetry or ServiceNow ITSM. Compare Datadog if you only need monitors+some incident UI; JSM if Atlassian ops alerting is enough.
editorialNotes: IT Priority-2 batch. Approved on it-development-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=incident-oncall. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Schedules and mobile paging are straightforward for SRE teams. Not a lab test.
Incident-oncall cluster — do not rank as an observability peer of Datadog.
Escalation, major-incident workflows, and status pages (plan-gated) are deep for paging; not ITIL CMDB depth.
Native hooks into Datadog, cloud, Slack/Teams are the product.
SSO and advanced admin rise on Business/Enterprise.
Unlimited responders on paid plans; add-ons scale cost.
$21 Professional is a clear floor; add-ons are the TCO trap. Affiliate economics excluded.
Advance/AIOps are add-ons, not included intelligence on Professional.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the eight IT editorial criteria using category weights (IT job fit 16, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, admin/security 12, value 12, AI 12, scalability 10), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ITSM, observability, source control, hosting panels, and web-data platforms are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
